verdict.rationale: Customer.io's official MCP server lets an agent create and manage automations and one-time sends and work with segments. Its docs also say the AI can draft messages, and broadcasts can be queued for a specified time. The MCP read/write permission separation is a tool-call approval in the AI client, not a campaign approval gate. No documented draft-awaiting-approval state or human sign-off step before send exists. missing for 10: documented draft/pending-approval state for agent-created campaigns, human approval workflow before send, evidence that agent-created sends can be left scheduled rather than sent, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can draft a campaign against a segment and leave it scheduled or queued for a human to approve before send

citations.quote: create and manage automations and one-time sends, work with segments, and more—all through natural language prompts
Broadcast messages are queued to send to all the defined recipients at a time you specify.
you can have it build automations, draft messages, analyze performance, and so on
